question: Why do larger departures from the mean influence variance more than smaller departures?
direct_answer: Because deviations are squared before averaging.
expanded_answer: Squaring makes each deviation grow faster than linearly as it gets larger. This means a few large outliers can raise variance a lot, which is useful when you want spread to reflect extreme variation rather than just average distance.
common_wrong_ideas: Only the number of points, not their size, affects variance
